question: When was the 48th edition of the Paris Marathon held?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Apr 13 **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Paris Marathon**, officially known as the Schneider Electric Marathon de Paris, is one of the most popular and prestigious annual running events in the world.
 
• The **48th edition** of the Paris Marathon is scheduled to be held on **April 13, 2026**. This date is confirmed as per the event's calendar, aligning with traditional scheduling in spring.
 
• The marathon typically takes place in **April**, making it a prominent springtime event that attracts participants globally.
 
• The event covers a distance of **42.195 kilometers**, starting from the Champs-Élysées and ending at Avenue Foch, providing scenic views of iconic Parisian landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower and Notre Dame Cathedral.
 
• Participants from various categories, including professionals and amateur runners, compete in this marathon, which is recognized for its festive atmosphere and large number of participants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of Paris Marathon:**

 
 
• The Paris Marathon began in **1976**, making it one of the oldest city marathons in the world.
 
• It has grown significantly over the years, with participation levels often exceeding **50,000 runners**.
 
• The marathon is organized by Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO), a renowned organizer of sporting events.
 
 
 
• **Route and Highlights:**
 
 
• The marathon route is designed to showcase **Paris’s cultural heritage** and scenic beauty, passing landmarks like the Place de la Concorde, Bois de Vincennes, and Bois de Boulogne.
 
• Runners experience a combination of urban landscapes and natural surroundings, making the event unique compared to other marathons.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility and Participation:**
 
 
• The marathon is open to runners aged **20 years and above**, per the guidelines of the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).
 
• Participants must register in advance, and the event often reaches full capacity due to high demand.
 
• The Paris Marathon is known for its diverse participation, attracting runners from over **140 countries**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Paris Marathon incorporates sustainability efforts, including waste management and the use of eco-friendly materials for race supplies.
 
• Participants are encouraged to reduce their environmental impact by using public transport and minimizing waste during the event.
 
 
 
• **Training and Preparation:**
 
 
• Runners typically follow training programs that span **16-20 weeks** to prepare for the marathon's physical demands.
 
• Nutrition, hydration, and pacing strategies are critical for successfully completing the marathon.
 
• Many participants use this event as an opportunity to raise funds for **charitable causes**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Significance:** The Paris Marathon is ranked among the top international marathons, alongside the Boston, London, and New York City marathons.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The event contributes significantly to Paris’s economy, attracting tourists, generating revenue for local businesses, and creating jobs.
 
• **Registration Process:** Registration for the marathon typically opens several months in advance, and participants must pay an entry fee. Early registration often provides discounts.
 
• **Medical Facilities:** The marathon ensures comprehensive medical support, with stations set up along the route to assist runners in case of emergencies.
 
• **Charity Contributions:** Many participants use the marathon platform to support global and local charities, raising substantial funds through sponsorships and donations.
